items.q: Find the average rate of change of the drone's altitude from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 6</annotation></semantics></math> seconds. Include units.

mistakes.why: The quotient is upside down. A rate of change is change in altitude over change in time: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>47</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{47 - 14}{6 - 2}</annotation></semantics></math>.
That is the change in altitude, 33 meters. Divide by the change in time, 4 seconds, to get a rate.

That starts from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A(0) = 6</annotation></semantics></math> instead of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A(2) = 14</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>47</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{47 - 6}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>. Both the change in altitude and the change in time must use <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 6</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>47</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{47 - 14}{6 - 2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Which sentence correctly interprets <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>8.25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{A(6) - A(2)}{6 - 2} = 8.25</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: Between <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 6</annotation></semantics></math> seconds, the altitude rose 8.25 meters per second on average.

At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 4</annotation></semantics></math> seconds, the drone was rising at exactly 8.25 meters per second.

The drone climbed a total of 8.25 meters between <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 6</annotation></semantics></math> seconds.

Between <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 6</annotation></semantics></math> seconds, the drone was 8.25 meters above the street.

items.q: Over which interval of the table was the average rate of change of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> greatest?

A student says the drone was rising at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>41</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>8.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{A(5)}{5} = \frac{41}{5} = 8.2</annotation></semantics></math> meters per second at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 5</annotation></semantics></math>. What is wrong with this reasoning?
options: It divides an altitude by a time instead of dividing a change in altitude by a change in time.
It should divide by 6 seconds, the next time in the table.
Nothing; an altitude divided by its time is the rate at that time.

It should use <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A(9)</annotation></semantics></math>, the last altitude, because more data gives a better rate.

mistakes.why: Check the expansion: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(1 + h)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{(1 + h)^2}{2} - (1 + h) + 2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1.5</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1.5 + \frac{h^2}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. The <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+h</annotation></semantics></math> from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>h</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2h}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> cancels the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-h</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(1 + h) - f(1)</annotation></semantics></math>, the numerator. Divide it by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>.

Type an expression in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>h</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2 + h)^2 = 4 + 4h + h^2</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4 + h^2</annotation></semantics></math>. With the middle term, the numerator is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^2 + 7h</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is the limit as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h \to 0</annotation></semantics></math>. The quotient itself still contains <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mi>h</mi></mrow><mi>h</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{h^2 + 7h}{h} = 7 + h</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(2)</annotation></semantics></math>, the value of the function. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(-1)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-1)^4 = 1</annotation></semantics></math>: an even power of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math> is positive, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5(-1)^4 = 5</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(-1)</annotation></semantics></math>, the height. The slope is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(-1) = 5(-1)^4</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: For which function does the power rule NOT give the derivative, even after rewriting?

Rewrite <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \frac{1}{x}</annotation></semantics></math> as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> and use the power rule. Which line is tangent to this hyperbola where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math>?

At what value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> does the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \sqrt{x}</annotation></semantics></math> have slope <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>?

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{x}</annotation></semantics></math>. From <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} = \frac{1}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{x} = 3</annotation></semantics></math>, so square: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 9</annotation></semantics></math>.

The slope is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}</annotation></semantics></math>, with a 2: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\sqrt{x} = 6</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{x} = 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>10</mn></msup><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dx}\left( x^{10} \right)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Bring the 10 down and lower the exponent by one: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>9</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{9}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The exponent 10 also comes down as a coefficient: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>9</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10x^9</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: A student writes <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dx}\left( \frac{1}{x^4} \right) = \frac{1}{4x^3}</annotation></semantics></math>. What is the correct derivative?

What is the slope of the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = x^4</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -2</annotation></semantics></math>?

Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = \frac{x^3 \cdot x^4}{x^2}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ne 0</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(x)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That differentiates each piece separately: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3x^2 \cdot 4x^3}{2x}</annotation></semantics></math>. Simplify first: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x^3 \cdot x^4}{x^2} = x^5</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x)</annotation></semantics></math> simplified. Now apply the power rule.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(x)</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x + 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The constant term 1 has derivative 0; it does not combine with the 9.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>6</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dx}\left( 6x^2 \right) = 6 \cdot 2x = 12x</annotation></semantics></math>: keep the constant factor and bring the exponent down.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>9</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dx}(9x) = 9</annotation></semantics></math>, not 0. Only the constant term disappears.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(2)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>24</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>18</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(2) = 8 - 24 + 18 + 1</annotation></semantics></math>, the height. The slope is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(2) = 3(4) - 12(2) + 9</annotation></semantics></math>.
The constant 1 was kept in the derivative; its derivative is 0.

items.q: At which values of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> is the line tangent to the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> level (slope 0)?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -3</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Which is an equation of the line tangent to the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>?

Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(x) = 3f(x) - 2g(x)</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h'(2)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(2) = 3(3) - 2(5)</annotation></semantics></math>, built from the values. Use the derivative columns: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3f'(2) - 2g'(2)</annotation></semantics></math>.

The minus sign applies to the whole <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2g'(2)</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3(-1) - 2(4) = -3 - 8</annotation></semantics></math>.

Keep the constant factors: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(3f)' = 3f'</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2g)' = 2g'</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3(-1) - 2(4)</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k(x) = f(x) + g(x) + 7</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k'(4)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The constant 7 has derivative 0: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k'(4) = f'(4) + g'(4)</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k(4) = 0 + (-1) + 7</annotation></semantics></math>. Use <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(4)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g'(4)</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(x) = 5f(x) - x^2</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p'(2)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Keep the factor 5: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dx}\left( 5f(x) \right) = 5f'(x)</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5(-1) - 2(2)</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(2) = 5(3) - 4</annotation></semantics></math>. Use the derivative: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5f'(2) - 2(2)</annotation></semantics></math>.

The term <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-x^2</annotation></semantics></math> has derivative <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2x</annotation></semantics></math>, which is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-4</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+4</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5(-1) - 4 = -9</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Which is an equation of the line tangent to the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(x) = 3f(x) - 2g(x)</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math>?

Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 4x^3 - \frac{5}{x} + 2\sqrt{x}</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{5}{x} = -5x^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> has derivative <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-5(-1)x^{-2} = +\frac{5}{x^2}</annotation></semantics></math>: two negatives make a positive.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\sqrt{x} = 2x^{1/2}</annotation></semantics></math> has derivative <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2 \cdot \frac{1}{2}x^{-1/2} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}</annotation></semantics></math>; the 2 and the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> cancel.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dx}\left( (x^2 + 1)^2 \right)</annotation></semantics></math> by expanding first.

mistakes.why: The power rule is for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^n</annotation></semantics></math>, not for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x^2 + 1)^n</annotation></semantics></math>. Expand: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x^2 + 1)^2 = x^4 + 2x^2 + 1</annotation></semantics></math>, then differentiate term by term.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dx}\left( 2x^2 \right) = 4x</annotation></semantics></math>: the factor 2 stays.

The constant 1 has derivative 0, and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x^2</annotation></semantics></math> has derivative <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4x</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \frac{x^3 - 2x}{x}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ne 0</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That differentiates the numerator and the denominator separately (<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mn>1</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3x^2 - 2}{1}</annotation></semantics></math>). Divide first: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x^3 - 2x}{x} = x^2 - 2</annotation></semantics></math>.
That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> simplified. Now differentiate it.

At what value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> does the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = x^2 - 6x + 4</annotation></semantics></math> have slope 2?

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x - 6 = 2</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x = 8</annotation></semantics></math>; divide by 2.
